name: Pulmonary Arteriovenous Malformations

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Curaçao Criteria (for Hereditary Hemorrhagic Telangiectasia-related PAVMs)

criteria.description: Presence of one or more pulmonary arteriovenous malformations confirmed by contrast-enhanced chest CT or pulmonary angiography
Evidence of hypoxemia or right-to-left shunting demonstrated by arterial blood gas analysis or contrast echocardiography
Associated clinical features such as dyspnea, cyanosis, or clubbing
Family history of hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia or PAVMs

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Radiologic evidence of PAVMs plus either hypoxemia or clinical features consistent with right-to-left shunting
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is often supported by genetic testing if hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia is suspected.

pathognomonic.notes: Central cyanosis due to right-to-left shunting

common.notes: May indicate rupture or bleeding from PAVMs

occasional.symptomName: Neurological deficits due to paradoxical emboli
occasional.notes: Stroke or brain abscess secondary to right-to-left shunting
Common in hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia-associated cases
May occur with PAVM rupture or high-output cardiac failure

rare.notes: Due to large or multiple PAVMs
Secondary to cerebral ischemia or abscess

laboratory: Arterial blood gas showing hypoxemia with normal or low PaCO2
imaging: Contrast-enhanced chest CT showing direct pulmonary artery to vein connections
genetic: Mutations in ENG, ACVRL1, or SMAD4 genes in hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia-associated cases
other: Bubble contrast echocardiography positive for intrapulmonary shunting
Physical exam findings such as digital clubbing and cyanosis

distinguishingFeatures: Family history of autosomal dominant inheritance
Acute onset dyspnea and chest pain
Absence of direct artery-to-vein malformations on imaging
Elevated D-dimer and evidence of thrombus

redFlags: Neurological symptoms suggestive of stroke or brain abscess
Severe hypoxemia refractory to oxygen therapy
references: Shovlin CL. Pulmonary arteriovenous malformations. Am J Respir Crit Care Med. 2014;190(11):1217-1228.
Curaçao Criteria for diagnosis of hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia. Am J Med Genet. 1999;83(1):1-7.
Faughnan ME, et al. Pulmonary arteriovenous malformations: diagnosis and treatment. Chest. 2011;140(3):1033-1044.
